claims.claim: Beating and the double decay come from interference of two coupled modes with different decay rates; detuning of the unison strings (mistuning) shapes the beat rate and envelope. A model that merely sums two slightly detuned lossless-coupled strings gives beating but not a genuine two-stage decay; the second, longer-lived component needs strings that couple through a lossy bridge admittance (sym/antisym modes with different Q).

summary: Fetch was unavailable for every host, so all sources are search-summary level and nothing is marked corroborated. Verified by own calculation: the input's mandolin B/cents table is arithmetically exact; B = pi^3 E d^4/(64 T L^2) derived, plus f0/mu forms. Woodhouse 2021 exists (JASA 150(6), 4375-4384, DOI 10.1121/10.0009012, arXiv 2104.02480); abstract says lute and mandolin show double decay over much of the range, especially higher. Input's 500 Hz mandolin threshold, +/-8 cents and modal-overlap statements were NOT found; eta_b >> eta_air is stronger than the relayed 'necessary condition'. Perng thesis exists (Stanford 2012); Germain and Evangelista DAFx 2009 title not found. End-correction 0.6-0.85 is per-radius per-end (about 1.7 r for a thin-plate hole). Tremolo, T60 data, and loss-factor values remain open.
